title: Mediation Act s. 20 — Mediated settlement agreement (Registration & Finality) (Mediation s. 20)

content.overview: Section 20 of the Mediation Act, 2023 provides for registration of a mediated settlement agreement. It is not the section that defines the agreement, enforces it, or lists challenge grounds. The mediated settlement agreement itself is s. 19. Registration under s. 20 is the recording step with the authority or body and in the manner prescribed. Enforcement of a mediated settlement agreement is s. 27. A challenge lies under s. 28 on the stated grounds, within the limitation in s. 29. The topic title's reference to finality must be read with that map: registration does not by itself replace enforcement or the challenge window.
content.glance: Mediation Act s. 20 — Mediated settlement agreement (Registration & Finality) (Mediation s. 20). Complete ADR treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Keep four sections apart: s. 19 formation and signature, s. 20 registration, s. 27 enforcement, s. 28 challenge. A problem about whether the settlement can be executed is a s. 27 problem. A problem about fraud or a First Schedule matter is a s. 28 problem.

learningObjectives: Place s. 20 as the registration provision, not the definition or enforcement provision.
Connect registration to the s. 19 agreement and the s. 27 enforcement route.
Avoid treating registration as a bar to a s. 28 challenge.
enhancement.definition: Section 20 provides for registration of a mediated settlement agreement. The agreement is defined and authenticated under s. 19; it is enforced under s. 27 and may be challenged under s. 28.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Registration is a recording mechanism. Enforceability and finality are governed by the enforcement and challenge sections, not by the mere fact of registration.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Mediation Act, 2023, s. 20; mediated settlement agreement in s. 19; enforcement in s. 27; challenge in s. 28; limitation in s. 29. Registration mechanics depend on rules under the Act.
essentialIngredients: A mediated settlement agreement within s. 19
Registration step under s. 20 in the prescribed manner
Enforcement analysed under s. 27, not assumed from registration
Challenge grounds and forum analysed under s. 28
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The enacted contents place registration in s. 20, after the mediated settlement agreement in s. 19 and before the non-settlement report in s. 21. Chapter VI then deals with enforcement (s. 27) and challenge (s. 28). A teaching note that treats s. 20 as the finality section misstates the Act. Registration may evidence the agreement and support later enforcement, but a party who alleges fraud, corruption, impersonation, or mediation of a matter not fit under s. 6 uses the s. 28 application. Whether a particular registration rule or Council infrastructure has been notified must be checked; this note does not invent a registration form or fee.
examples: Parties sign a s. 19 settlement and register it under s. 20, then seek enforcement under s. 27.
A registered settlement is later challenged for impersonation; the forum and grounds are s. 28, not a second registration.
No settlement is reached; the correct instrument is a non-settlement report under s. 21, not registration under s. 20.
enhancement.problemApplication: Ask whether an agreement under s. 19 exists; whether registration is pleaded; whether the relief sought is enforcement or challenge. Apply s. 27 or s. 28 accordingly. Do not dismiss a fraud challenge only because the agreement was registered.

Registration is not pleaded as a substitute for a lawful s. 19 agreement.
